fdroid:com.norsehorse.scrubpony.name: ScrubPony
fdroid:com.norsehorse.scrubpony.summary: Strip GPS and metadata from JPEG, PNG, WebP and HEIC photos, on your device.
fdroid:com.norsehorse.scrubpony.description:
ScrubPony removes the hidden metadata from your photos while leaving the picture itself untouched.
Phones write a lot into every photo you take: GPS coordinates, the exact date and time, the camera and phone model, and small embedded thumbnails. ScrubPony strips those out and writes a fresh, clean copy. The image data is copied through byte for byte, so the photo looks exactly the same.
It works on JPEG, PNG, WebP and HEIC, including the HEICs most phone cameras save by default. Pick one photo or a whole batch.
Everything happens on your device. Nothing is uploaded, no network is used, and the app asks for no permissions. Your original files are never changed. Every scrub produces a new copy that you can save to your gallery, save to any folder, or share straight to another app. You can also share photos into ScrubPony from any other app's share sheet.
The metadata handling is the same C core as the desktop ScrubPony, compiled into the app. It is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

fdroid:com.sleepsecret.sleep_secret.name: Sleep Secret
fdroid:com.sleepsecret.sleep_secret.summary: Record the night, classify sounds on-device, get a morning report.
fdroid:com.sleepsecret.sleep_secret.description:
Record the night, classify the sounds in it on your phone, and get a report in the morning: when there was sound, what it was, and how long it lasted.
Audio stays on the device by default. There is no account and no server — install it and it works. The only exception is if you configure your own WebDAV storage in the export screen; after that, each night's results are uploaded to a drive under your own name.
Recognition runs on the phone. The model is CED-tiny (5.5M parameters, pretrained on AudioSet), converted to ONNX and run on-device. It does not need a network connection.
What it does
- Night-long sound timeline: when there was sound, what it was, how long it lasted
- Snore index: snoring time as a percentage of analysed time, for comparing one night to another
- Category breakdown and hourly distribution
- Event details: time, category and confidence for each event. Snoring clips can be played back inline, with a waveform and a draggable seek bar
The nine categories it reports: snoring / breathing / cough and throat clearing / sneeze / voice and sleep talking / body movement and bed noise / environmental noise / device noise / silence.
What it does not do
- It is not a medical device and cannot be used to diagnose sleep apnoea or any other condition
- It does not do sleep staging (light / deep / REM). That needs movement or heart rate; audio alone cannot do it
- It does not keep the raw audio of the whole night (8 hours is roughly 920 MB). What is kept is the timing and category of each event, plus any snoring clips you choose to retain
Android only for phones; there is also a Windows build intended for testing. There is no iOS version.
Free software under the GPL-3.0-or-later. Source code: https://github.com/14790897/sleep-secret

fdroid:eu.veldsoft.no.thanks.name: No Thanks!
fdroid:eu.veldsoft.no.thanks.summary: No Thanks! is a popular card game
fdroid:eu.veldsoft.no.thanks.description:
No Thanks! is a card game created by Thorsten Gimmler, ideal for groups of three to seven players. Originally known as Geschenkt!, it was first published by Amigo Spiele in 2004 and later translated into English by Z-Man Games.
Card Range: The game features playing cards numbered from 3 to 35. Before the game begins, nine cards are randomly selected and removed from the deck, which is then thoroughly shuffled.
Chips Distribution: The number of chips each player receives at the start of the game depends on the player count. With 3 to 5 players, each player begins with 11 chips. For 6 players, each starts with 9 chips, and in games with 7 players, each player receives 7 chips. Players also have the option to conceal their chips from others if they wish.
Game Initiation: The first player initiates the game by revealing the top card from the shuffled deck. They have a choice: they can either take the card, accumulating points according to its value, or opt to pass on it by paying a chip, which is then placed on the card. The player must declare "No thanks!" when passing. Subsequently, play continues in a clockwise direction, with each player making the same decision when their turn arrives.
Collecting Cards and Chips: The gameplay continues until a player decides to take the card along with all the chips accumulated on it, if any. The player who accepts the card then flips over the next card and repeats the process, deciding whether to take it or pass it. This pattern persists until all the cards in the deck have been taken.
Scoring: In the final scoring phase of the game, players calculate their points based on the values of the cards they have collected. Notably, cards in a consecutive run are treated as a single card with the lowest value. For example, a run of cards with numbers 30, 29, 28, and 27 would be considered a 27-point set. Each chip held by a player incurs a negative point, resulting in a strategic consideration to minimize the number of chips you accumulate.
Victory: The player or players with the lowest overall point total win the game. Mastering the art of minimizing card values and judicious chip management are key strategies for success in No Thanks!

fdroid:io.github.bropines.tailscaled.name: TailSocks
fdroid:io.github.bropines.tailscaled.summary: Unofficial Tailscale client: local SOCKS5/HTTP proxy, optional VPN, root mode
fdroid:io.github.bropines.tailscaled.description:
TailSocks is an unofficial client for Tailscale networks (tailnets). It runs the Tailscale daemon in userspace-networking mode and gives your apps the tailnet through local SOCKS5 and HTTP proxies, so it does not take Android's VPN slot and runs next to another VPN, firewall or ad blocker. When you want system-wide routing, a VPN (TUN) mode is one switch away.
It works with Tailscale's own coordination server and with a self-hosted Headscale server.
 Networking 
• Local SOCKS5 proxy (optional username and password) and HTTP proxy, optionally reachable from your local network
• VPN (TUN) mode: full or split tunnel, per-app exclusions, accepted subnet routes; the daemon runs the tunnel itself, with hev-socks5-tunnel as a compatibility engine
• Exit nodes; MagicDNS and split DNS through a local DNS server, with a DNS-over-HTTPS fallback
• Root mode (experimental): a kernel tailscale0 interface with policy routing that steps aside when another VPN app holds the VPN slot
• Restricted networks: send coordination traffic through your own SOCKS5/HTTP proxy, or through the built-in ByeDPI against SNI-based DPI
• Optional auto-reconnect, a watchdog for a killed service, and start after reboot
 Services and files 
• Taildrop: send and receive files, including from the share sheet
• Taildrive: share folders and open the shares of other devices. The daemon reads a shared folder itself, so sharing one asks for All files access; nothing else does
• Serve and Funnel, Tailscale Services (svc:)
• TailCat: forward ports or run a SOCKS5 proxy through a tailcat server, with no VPN and no Tailscale account; the phone can serve its own ports too
 Management 
• Several accounts, each with its own state, keys and settings
• A console for the Tailscale Admin API (devices, DNS, users, auth keys, ACLs), protected by a biometric lock
• Encrypted backups and per-account export
• Automation: token-protected broadcast intents for Tasker or MacroDroid, and Android AppFunctions on Android 16+
• Home-screen widgets, a Quick Settings tile, network diagnostics (netcheck, DERP latency)
• Material 3 with dynamic colour and AMOLED black; English and Russian
 Network access 
The app talks to the coordination server you choose (Tailscale's by default), to DERP relays and to your peers. Names outside the tailnet are resolved through 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1, with Cloudflare's DNS-over-HTTPS (https://1.1.1.1/dns-query) as the fallback; all of them can be changed in Settings. TailCat, when you switch it on, fetches its relay map from tailcat.dev and connects through Tailscale's public DERP relays. The Tailscale Admin API is contacted only after you add an API token. Upload of debug logs to Tailscale is compiled out. Checking GitHub for a newer release on launch is a setting you can turn off; builds distributed through a store have it off.
 Requirements 
Android 7.0 or newer and an account on Tailscale or on a Headscale server. Root is optional.

fdroid:org.blitzortung.android.app.description:
Simple to use map based application, visualizing real time full area lightning data provided by the blitzortung.org lightning location network project. The current thunderstorm situation at your fingertips.
 Features: 
* realtime display of lightning data
* display of historical lightning data of the last 24 hours
* for regions Europe, North & South America, Asia, Africa and Australia/New Zealand
* lightning strike time color coded
* reduced data volume and fast response
* current lightning strike time and lightning count
* optional user location marker
* alert function shows distance/direction of storms
* background service for alerts
* support for notifications, sound and vibration alarm
* single stroke display for blitzortung.org participants
Please visit https://www.blitzortung.org for more information regarding the community based lightning location project.
The raster display ensures a fast performance of the application even if there is a very high thunderstorm activity. Blitzortung.org participants can visualize all stroke locations individually.
If you would like to contribute to a translation of the software in your language, please do not hesitate to contact the author of the software.
 User privacy
This app can use device location in order to show the users location on the map and for generating warning view and alerts for lightning activity nearby.
The lightning warning feature **can also be used without device location permissions** as the location can also be set manually (via preferences but also via long pressing the desired position on the map). You will still be able to use the warning feature without allowing location permissions.
In order to have a more efficient data transfer with high resolution lightning data the app only fetches the last 10 minutes of activity in an area of 5° x 5° rounded to five degrees.
Although this data is derived from the devices location or the map area currently visible it can not be used to track users.
Here is why:
 Granularity : A 5x5 degree area is extremely large.
 Latitude : 5 degrees covers approximately 555 km (345 miles).
 Longitude : At the equator, 5 degrees is also ~555 km. At 50° latitude (e.g., Central Europe/Canada), it is still ~355 km wide.
 This resolution is sufficient to identify a broad region (e.g., "Central Europe" or "US West Coast") but is completely insufficient to pinpoint a city, let alone a specific person or address.
 Anonymization : The calculation `(coordinate / scale).toInt()` effectively quantizes the location. All users within that massive 5x5 degree square report the exact same grid index (e.g., x=2, y=10). It is impossible to distinguish between two users within that same ~300,000 km² area based solely on these coordinates. On top of that, there is no data provided which would allow to link subsequent requests coming from the same app.
 Conclusion : The coordinates generated by `LocalData.update()` are too coarse for individual tracking. They serve only to download lightning data for the correct general region of the world.

WHAT IT FIXES
• Scratches and cracks. The app finds them on its own and heals the damage without touching the rest of the picture.

HOW AUTO RESTORE WORKS
One click runs the full pipeline in the right order: damage repair first, then noise and grain cleanup, then faces, then color, and upscaling last. Each step is a separate model trained for that one job, which is why the result looks restored rather than filtered. Prefer manual control? Toggle any step off and run only what the photo needs.
YOUR PHOTOS NEVER LEAVE YOUR IPHONE, IPAD, OR MAC
Most restoration apps upload your pictures to a server and put you in a queue. This one does not. Every model runs locally on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac, so a photo of your grandmother is processed on your computer and nowhere else. No account, no upload, no waiting. It works on a plane.
BUILT FOR REAL ARCHIVES
• Work through a single treasured portrait or a whole shoebox of scans. 
• Compare before and after with a split slider that shows the same area on both sides, down to the pixel. 
• Turn each fix on or off per photo: scratch removal, stain repair, face enhancement, colorization, upscaling. 
• History keeps every restoration with its settings, so you can return later and export again. 
• Opens JPEG, PNG, HEIC, TIFF, BMP, and WebP. Exports PNG, JPEG, or TIFF at full resolution, ready for print shops.
MADE FOR APPLE SILICON
The restoration models are tuned for the Neural Engine and GPU in M-series Macs. A typical 2000px scan is cleaned up in seconds; a full pass with faces and color usually finishes in under a minute.
WHO IT IS FOR
People digitizing family albums before the prints fade further. 
Genealogists attaching portraits to a family tree. 
Anyone who inherited a box of photographs and wants to see the faces in them clearly, maybe for the first time.
FREE AND PRO
Restoring and exporting a cleaned-up photo is free, so you can judge the quality on your own scans before paying anything. Pro unlocks 4x print resolution and the full toolkit, with a monthly plan, a yearly plan with a free trial, or a one-time lifetime purchase. No credits and no per-photo fees.

Monero is a private, secure, untraceable, decentralised digital currency. You
 are your bank, you control your funds, and nobody can trace your transfers
 unless you allow them to do so.
 Privacy: Monero uses a cryptographically sound system to allow you to send
 and receive funds without your transactions being easily revealed on the
 blockchain (the ledger of transactions that everyone has). This ensures that
 your purchases, receipts, and all transfers remain absolutely private by
 default.

 every transaction on the network is cryptographically secured. Individual
 wallets have a 25 word mnemonic seed that is only displayed once, and can be
 written down to backup the wallet. Wallet files are encrypted with a passphrase

gnome-extensions:talk2pc-focused-window@.name: Talk2PC Bridge: Voice Input, Presenter Remote & Phone Files
gnome-extensions:talk2pc-focused-window@.summary:
Your laptop microphone sounds bad, the system input method covers too few
languages, and typing is slow. Talk2PC routes input through your phone instead:
dictate, handwrite, or enter special characters on the phone, and the text is
written straight into the focused window. Phone microphones are usually better
and phone keyboards cover more languages and characters, so voice input,
handwriting, and write-as-you-translate work the way you are used to.
The phone also works as a wireless mouse and keyboard — tilt or swipe to move
the pointer while standing or walking. Send files to the computer, and keep the
clipboard in sync in both directions.
For teachers: photograph student work with the phone, then zoom, annotate and
explain it on the projector while controlling the slides. The presentation
pointer and spotlight overlay are drawn directly by this extension.
This extension is the GNOME Shell bridge for Talk2PC, not a standalone
application — installing it alone produces no visible interface. After you
install and run the Talk2PC desktop app from talk2pc.lycheenow.com, the
interface and all features are provided by the desktop and phone apps. The
extension itself only exposes interfaces on the session bus for focused-window
identity, pointer position, virtual keyboard and pointer injection, and area
screenshots. It opens no network ports and collects no telemetry.
Talk2PC does not implement the KDE Connect protocol, so it cannot be paired with
KDE Connect or GSConnect. It takes a different route: the desktop app talks to
this extension directly over the session bus.

And follow us on twitter: https://twitter.com/trockerapp 
More information:
You can trust Trocker! Trocker runs locally on your machine and does not send or receive any information from the Internet. It needs permission to all tabs in order to be able to detect and prevent any tracking images or tracked links from being loaded from any of the tabs. But it makes absolutely no outbound Internet access and we neither gather nor use any data about you or your browsing behavior.
Trocker is also open source with the source code available at https://github.com/trockerapp/trocker and we encourage everyone to check it out from there or from Chrome Dev tools to confirm that there are no suspicious activities being done.
Trocker keeps you safe in all webmails, including Gmail™, Yahoo! and Outlook.com . It has additional capabilities in Gmail, Inbox and Outlook.com . In these 3 webmails, it has a heuristic tracker detection that detects and blocks almost any email tracking attempt, even from not well-known trackers!
Trocker is very efficient as it only gets activated when a tracker is detected.
Technical details:
Some email trackers track emails by injecting an invisible small image in the mail that is hosted in a specific address in their server. They know when the email is opened by looking at the download requests of the injected images on their servers. 
Trocker (as a lovely Tracker Blocker) stops this by simply blocking those image links from being loaded. It finds those injected images by looking at the url and matching the url pattern with the tracking servers that host injected images.
If you yourself are a user of these tracking services (you track emails you send others), your service wouldn't be affected and will work fine. Trocker would only defend you from OTHERS tracking you.
Moreover, some links are click tracked meaning that if you click on them, your clicks are logged and tracked. Trocker tries to bypass those links and redirect you directly to the original target without you being tracked. If not possible, Trocker will inform you that the link you've clicked on is tracked.
No one will be able to know when and if you open their emails, or click on their links if you enable Trocker. In Gmail, Inbox and Outlook.com , Trocker has a heuristic tracker detection that will detect and block almost any tracker, even if it is unknown. This works based on the fact that very tiny images are almost always trackers. After all, if they want you to see the image, they will make it bigger than 1x1 pixel!

firefox-addons:2974192.summary: Adds a Download button under Facebook posts. One click opens GetFBVideo with the video ready to save as HD or SD MP4, or as MP3 audio. Matches light and dark mode and stays light on your computer.
firefox-addons:2974192.description:
Save Facebook videos straight from your feed, without copying links.
GetFBVideo adds a Download button to the action bar under each post, right next to Share. Click it and GetFBVideo opens in a new tab with that video already loading, so all that's left is choosing a format and saving it.
HOW IT WORKS
1. Scroll your feed as usual.
2. Click the Download button under a post.
3. Choose HD or SD (MP4), or MP3 for just the audio, and save.
FEATURES
• A Download button on posts in your feed, on Pages, in search results and on video pages
• Works in the Reels viewer too
• MP4 video in HD (when available) or SD, or MP3 audio only
• Looks like the buttons around it and follows light and dark mode
• Available in 19 languages, and opens GetFBVideo in your language
• Toolbar button: opens GetFBVideo, and loads the current video when you're on a video page
• No account or sign-up needed
LIGHT ON YOUR COMPUTER
• Only wakes up when new posts load, and pauses itself in background tabs
• No polling, no tracking, no ads in the add-on
• Asks for just two things: access to facebook.com to show the button, and activeTab for the toolbar button
PRIVACY
GetFBVideo collects no data. It doesn't store, share or sell anything about you or your browsing. The only thing it ever passes on is the link of the post you clicked Download on, which it opens on getfbvideo.pro at the moment you click.
GOOD TO KNOW
• Only public videos can be downloaded.
• Please download only videos you own or have permission to save, and respect the rights of the people who made them.
• Questions or feedback: https://getfbvideo.pro/contact
